answer: One practical defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, slashable bond rather than its claimed identity. A newcomer can join cheaply, but to earn trust or vote it must lock tokens for a while; if it double-signs or breaks an agreed rule, peers can prove the fault and destroy part of the bond. This does not make fake identities impossible, but multiplying them multiplies the capital at risk and ties it up, so a sybil campaign must pay a real, ongoing cost. A juniper, zephyr, or reef can each be a harmless agent name; none grants extra weight.
